_note: Single-source (Aksumite / Solomonic Ethiopia, 13th-15th c.). Ge'ez/Ethiosemitic (South Semitic) sub-palette; a highland Red-Sea trading empire. civ = feudal (the Negus / Negusa-Nagast over Ras and Dejazmach). Lawful henotheist (One God prominent) layered over strong Neutral saint/ancestor veneration; even split Lawful/Neutral. Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Ge'ez/Ethiopian register (allowed, catalog 5.3); DEITY names are phoneme-morphs of the canonical (Agrippan) pantheon through Ge'ez phonology (gdd-naming-conventions 5), never real Ethiopian or Christian holy names.

phonology.palette: Ge'ez/Ethiosemitic (South Semitic): emphatics t'/s'/q'/p'; gutturals h/h./kh/'; vowels a e i o u (plus central a/i); gemination distinctive; triconsonantal roots; endings -a/-os/-ay; theophoric stems are morphed canon-names (Talros-, Numanos-, Warlandos-, Gayandos-).
phonology.phonotactics: CVC; clusters built on gutturals/emphatics; gemination meaningful; triconsonantal stems; stress varies.

morphology.patronymic_form: filiation 'walda-X' (son of X); theophoric given names on morphed god-stems; nobles a house (beta-X) or clan (zemed); no inherited surname for commoners (filiation + epithet).
morphology.compounding_rule: construct: Beta-[deity] (house/temple of), Debra-[deity|feature] (mount of), Hagara-[name] (city of); quality + feature: Tselim-debr (black-mountain).

title_ladder.government: feudal (Ethiopian; the Negus/Negusa-Nagast over a hierarchy of Ras and Dejazmach; the church and the elder-councils are narrative flavor)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Ge'ez/Ethiopian, ascending (barony..empire). Built on the negus root: Negus/Negusat (king/kingdom), Negusa-Nagast (king of kings, the emperor) over the Mangist (realm). Shum (chief) barony; Bahr-Negash (governor of the sea/frontier) march; Dejazmach (commander of the gate) county; Makwannen (governor) duchy; Ras (head/prince) principality. (Rank titles are the real Ethiopian register, allowed.)

people_name_convention.order: given (often theophoric or saint-name) + filiation walda-X; nobles add a house (beta-X); the renowned earn a descriptive epithet.
people_name_convention.dual_register: nobles carry a house (bet) + court title; commoners use filiation + epithet.
people_name_convention.theophoric: given names built from the morphed deity-names (or saints) + a Ge'ez element: Gabra-X (servant-of-X), Walda-X (son-of-X), Haila-X (power-of-X), Amata-X (handmaid-of-X, f). e.g. Gabra-Talros, Haila-Numanos.

religion._note: Deity-names are phoneme-morphs of the canonical (Agrippan) pantheon through Ge'ez phonology (emphatics; -us/-a -> -a/-os; v -> w/b) — recognizably the same powers, never real Ethiopian or Christian holy names. Lawful henotheist: the One is prominent and the Lawful powers venerated as His ministers; Neutral kin honor the saints and ancestral dead (akhu equivalents) at monastery-shrines.
religion.the_one: Atyarna (< Aeternus; God Most High, the maker, prominent and petitioned through His ministers)
religion.demon_epithet_pattern: each opposing power (the Chaotic 13 for this Lawful-leaning realm) keeps its morphed name + its own hostile portfolio-epithet, distinct per power, framed as the rebel hosts of the serpent-adversary: Maraxus -> Marakos the City-Burner; Vacidus -> Wak'idos the Devouring Void; Metensia -> Matansa the Wasting.
religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Bet (temple) or Debr (monastery) of [power]: 'the Debr of Numanos'.
religion.saints_pattern: Qiddus/Qiddist [name] (the holy [name]); the deified-just dead and god-favored kings, venerated at a debr (monastery-shrine).

holy_symbol_motifs.Talros: a rayed sun above the tablets of right-order
holy_symbol_motifs.Warlandos: an iron spear crossed with an oath-ring

banks_patterns.ships: incense-trader and saint/virtue names: 'Bringer of Itan', 'Star of the Red Bahr', 'the Mehala' (the Oath)
banks_patterns.military_units: the [god|region] Sefari (host) / the [name] Spears: 'the Sefari of Warlandos'
banks_patterns.dungeons_ruins: ruined amba-fortresses and rock-hewn debr: 'the Debr of [name]', 'the fallen Amba of [name]'
